clue.text: Impresario slowly taking in capital

indicators.note: the phrase 'Impresario slowly' takes in, or holds within it, the letters of the answer across its word break

explanation.surface: A theatre producer, moving unhurriedly, drops by a capital city on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital sits across the join of impresariO SLOwly.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Extremely suggestive text sent to musicians

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, so only the ends of 'suggestive' are used
sent in the sense of sent into a whirl or disturbed, telling us to rearrange the letters of 'text'

explanation.surface: Someone fires off a racy message to a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives SE, the ends of suggestive; 'sent' turns TEXT into XTET.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group of six performers, so it is a body of musicians.

clue.text: Millions leaving real snowmen to melt in US city

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for millions departs from the pool of letters before it is rearranged
melting snowmen lose their shape, so the letters of 'real snowmen' are reformed into new order

explanation.surface: Genuine snowmen thawing away in an American city, where money has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M out of REALSNOWMEN and rearrange the remaining ten letters ('leaving', 'to melt').
explanation.definitionFit: New Orleans is a major city in Louisiana, in the United States.

clue.text: Crook caught at end of Ramadan in Asian sultanate

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in tells us the chosen letter is placed inside the name of the sultanate

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula in Asia

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here taken from 'Ramadan'

explanation.surface: A criminal is arrested as the Muslim fasting month ends in Oman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' Ramadan gives N, placed 'in' OMAN to give ONMAN, after C.
explanation.definitionFit: A conman is a swindler, the sort of criminal also called a crook.

clue.text: Dealer charged outside church taken in by cops

indicators.note: something taken in by a group is held within it, so the inner piece goes inside the word for the police

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: the word for charged sits outside, wrapping around, the abbreviation for church

parts.note: to charge is to rush or run, so charged gives ran

explanation.surface: A trader who rushed at a church is arrested by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police; 'charged' means rushed, not accused, and 'taken in by' reads as arrested but marks the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is a trader who buys and sells goods, so a dealer.

clue.text: Fish swallowing large lump of earth

indicators.note: a fish swallowing something takes it inside, so the letter for large goes within the fish

parts.note: cod is a common food fish
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A fish gulps down a big clump of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A clod is a lump of earth or clay, the dictionary sense of the word.

clue.text: Cambridge mathematician with right approach to resistance

parts.note: an angle is a way of approaching a problem
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A Cambridge maths student takes the correct line on resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: A wrangler is a student gaining first-class honours in the Cambridge University mathematics finals.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrangler is the traditional title for a first-class mathematics graduate at Cambridge University.

clue.text: Drink from California and Virginia

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of California
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A wine imported from two American states.
explanation.definitionFit: Cava is a Spanish sparkling wine, so a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Deserve to operate as a dockside worker

indicators.note: to operate on something is to work it over, so the letters of 'Deserve to' are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone earns the right to work as a docker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships, a labourer at the docks.

clue.text: Spanish poet coming from Mallorca

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the island's name, its letters lying in sequence within it

explanation.surface: A Spanish poet hails from the island of Majorca.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet's name ends the island's name, malLORCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico García Lorca was a celebrated twentieth-century Spanish poet and dramatist.

clue.text: Best alfresco function?

parts.note: alfresco means outdoors, in the open air, so out
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: Asks whether the finest event is a garden party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat or surpass them, the same as outperforming them.

clue.text: Scotsman and journalist together working initially in a part of Greece

parts.note: Mac is a familiar address for a Scotsman
ED is short for editor, a journalist
on means working or functioning, as a machine is on

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A Scot and a newspaperman labour side by side in a Greek region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'together' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia is a region of northern Greece, a part of the country.

clue.text: Silver coin in tin belonging to someone from Barcelona?

indicators.note: in places the coin within the word for tin

parts.note: a can is a tin container
the tala is the currency unit and coin of Samoa

explanation.surface: A silver coin found inside a can belongs to a Barcelonan.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: not everyone from Barcelona is Catalan, but a Barcelonan is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is the capital of Catalonia, so its people are Catalans.

clue.text: Head of sport leaving great magazine

indicators.note: leaving says the chosen letter departs from the word for great

parts.note: cosmic means vast or great

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here from 'sport'

explanation.surface: A sports editor quits a great magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' sport is S; 'leaving' takes it from COSMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic is a periodical of strip cartoons, a kind of magazine.

clue.text: EU slang involved in a Catholic prayer

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Brussels jargon is worked into a Catholic prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion recited morning, noon and evening, marked by a bell.

clue.text: Snigger about raised surface of biscuit

indicators.note: about means around in disorder, so the letters of 'Snigger' are moved about

parts.note: nap is the raised pile on the surface of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone giggles at the raised texture on a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingersnap is a crisp ginger-flavoured cookie, a type of biscuit.

clue.text: Fibre taken from new sails

indicators.note: new signals the letters of 'sails' are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fibre stripped from freshly made sails.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Hornby's construction system missing no place in Saudi Arabia

indicators.note: missing says the word 'no' is lacking from the toy's name

parts.note: Meccano is the metal construction toy invented by Frank Hornby

explanation.surface: A toy-maker's construction set is lost somewhere in Saudi Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: Meccano is a British model construction kit of metal strips and nuts and bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mecca is the holy city in western Saudi Arabia, a place there.

clue.text: Riddles about Pluto absorbing artist

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the artist goes inside the underworld

parts.note: Pluto is the Roman god of the underworld, the Greek Hades
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Puzzles concerning a god of the dead swallowing a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades are word puzzles, riddles in which syllables are acted or described.

clue.text: Maggot first in beef to turn

indicators.note: the first in a word is its opening letter, here from 'beef'
turn says the word 'to' is turned round end to end

explanation.surface: A grub, first found in meat, starts to rot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bot is the larva of the botfly, a maggot that infests animals.

clue.text: Cowboy's money put on a jumper

parts.note: buck is slang for a dollar, money
a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

explanation.surface: A cowboy's cash is bet on a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater, a British sense, but here it is a leaping kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckaroo is American slang for a cowboy, from the Spanish vaquero.

clue.text: Informers with partners impounding ship

indicators.note: impounding means shutting in, so the ship is enclosed by the partners

parts.note: N and S, North and South, are partners at bridge
an ark is a ship, as Noah's

explanation.surface: Police informants and their accomplices seize a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nark is British slang for a police informer, a grass.

clue.text: First-class seminar on one chapter

parts.note: a seminar is a class or teaching session
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An excellent seminar about a single chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Classic means of the highest quality, outstanding, as first-rate.

clue.text: Head of urology given endlessly stretchy tool

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here from 'urology'
endlessly means the last letter is cut off the word for stretchy

parts.note: tensile means capable of being stretched

explanation.surface: A senior urologist is handed a flexible instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, especially one used in the kitchen.

clue.text: Nudity abroad is out of order

indicators.note: abroad means widely scattered or astray, so the letters of 'Nudity' are spread into new order

explanation.surface: Nakedness overseas is improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' reads as improper conduct, but means disordered, messy.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy means disorganised, not in its proper arrangement.

clue.text: Southern sailors going north catch first of piranha fish

indicators.note: catch means trap inside, so the chosen letter goes within the other pieces
in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: tars are sailors

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of 'piranha'

explanation.surface: Seamen in the south heading north land a piranha.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' reverses S+TARS to SRATS; 'catch' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprats are small herring-like sea fish, so the plural noun matches fish.

clue.text: Advantage gained by Dutch champion during preliminary race

indicators.note: during says these pieces come inside, within the span of, the race

parts.note: a heat is a preliminary round of a race
a star is an outstanding performer, a champion

explanation.surface: A Dutch sprinter wins an edge in an early qualifying race.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an advantage given or gained at the beginning.

clue.text: Old horse's kick

definitions.meaning: a worn-out horse, or one let out for hire
to kick an opponent's shins, as in football

explanation.surface: A worn-out nag lashes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hack names a tired horse and also means to kick at the legs.

clue.text: Boozer drinking hooch finally fired

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the letter goes inside the drunkard

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard, a boozer

indicators.note: finally signals the last letter of 'hooch'

explanation.surface: A drunk downs the last of the moonshine and is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' could be a British pub, but here it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot is the past tense of shoot, so fired as a gun is.

clue.text: Axe stunted trees

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan is to cancel or axe it
land covered with low stunted trees and bushes

explanation.surface: Chop down the dwarf trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrub means to cancel a plan and also low scrubby vegetation.

clue.text: Bishop put on garment over part of nun's habit

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: over says the word for the garment is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment

explanation.surface: A bishop dresses in some item over a nun's robes.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a pleated linen cloth covering a nun's chin and throat.

clue.text: Catholic about to practise set of beliefs

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to do is to practise or perform

explanation.surface: A Catholic rehearses a creed.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a statement of the principles one holds.

clue.text: Clumsy model sat for Rembrandt's first great painting

indicators.note: clumsy means badly put together, so the letters are reassembled
first means the opening letter of 'Rembrandt's'

explanation.surface: An awkward sitter posed for Rembrandt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rembrandt's first' supplies the final R; 'great painting' fits Rembrandt himself, one of the old masters.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a great European painting from before about 1800.
